messages:
ade: quick question — we keep debating whether the fanout scorer should live in the policy compile path or be instantiated at runtime. what are the practical tradeoffs for latency/cold-starts and telemetry? :thinking:
chris: TL;DR: compile-time scorers are fast at eval time but make hot-reload & tenant rollouts painful. runtime scorers are flexible but add per-request overhead unless cached.
mari: adding some concrete numbers — if we allocate scorer instances per-route on demand, warmup is ~35ms on p3-sized machines for our python-based scorers. compiled static scorers (C++) are ~4–6ms.
piotr: also note memory: compiled scorers get shared memory for lookup tables, runtime per-tenant instances blow up RAM if we naively keep one-per-tenant.
ade: right — but runtime allows per-tenant overrides and quick feature flags. can we get the best of both? thought: keep scorer graph compiled but allow small runtime adapters that are scriptable and sandboxed.
samir: +1. propose an adapter interface: ``ScorerAdapter(name, evaluate_fn, lifecycle={shared|tenant|request})``. adapters can be hot-reloaded and bound to a compiled scorer via a stable ID.
mari: that sounds ok. need to consider cache invalidation for prefix/KV cache when adapter behavior changes. we don't want silent quality regressions.
piotr: telemetry: we should record adapter fingerprint (hash of code + config) and include that in spans and eval logs. then we can correlate quality regressions to adapter changes.
rachelle: ops-bot noted deploy: "ops-bot: deploy started: scorer-adapter-hotreload v0.3 -> staging". ops-bot: :rocket:
ops-bot: deploy status: staging passed, canary in prod scheduled for 2am UTC.
chris: rollout policy idea — default to compiled scorer; if a tenant has an override, attach a runtime adapter but put it behind a sampling guard (1% traffic) until evals pass. increase sample on metric stability.
ade: what evals exactly? we should define a small prompt set and quality thresholds (delta BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-sim). also latency percentiles and p99 budget.
samir: propose eval harness: run 1k queries through the adapter in a sandbox, compare outputs vs baseline compiled scorer, compute similarity and latency deltas. add automatic regression alerts if quality drops > 2% or p99 latency increases > 20ms.
mari: operational concern: if many tenants enable runtime adapters simultaneously, we could OOM. need admission control: `max_runtime_adapters` per region + LRU eviction of inactive tenant adapters.
piotr: config sketch:
```
scorer_pool:
  max_adapters: 500
  eviction_policy: lru
  cold_start_policy: prefetch_on_probe
```
ade: nice. also add a "graceful degrade" path where if a runtime adapter fails or times out, we fallback to the compiled scorer automatically. include fallback counters for SLA dashboards.
rachelle: action items?
chris: 1) write a short RFC for "hybrid scorer runtime" with adapter API and hot-reload safety. 2) add eval harness prototype (samir + mari) 3) implement telemetry fingerprint and SPA (piotr + ade) 4) ops to add admission control knobs (rachelle). 5) run a small canary rollout with 3 tenants.
ade: I'll draft the RFC and include the config sketch + handoff checklist for canary. aiming for RFC by EOD Fri.
samir: I'll prototype the harness this week.
mari: I'll add memory simulations and p99 test.
piotr: I'll draft the fingerprint + span schema.
rachelle: ops will schedule the canary window and add alerts for adapter OOM and fallback rate.
achieved: decision for now: go hybrid — default compiled, runtime adapters allowed with strict admission and eval gates.
ade: thanks all. moving this to RFC channel when draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
